text:
Head of Regulatory Affairs – Calloway Biosciences

Calloway Biosciences, a mid-sized developer of diagnostic devices, is seeking an experienced Head of Regulatory Affairs to lead a team of eleven specialists across three sites. The successful candidate will be accountable for securing market authorization in the European Union and North America and will [1] closely with the quality and clinical departments.

[2] You will be expected to anticipate changes in legislation rather than merely respond to them, and to advise the executive board on their commercial implications. Applicants should hold a degree in a scientific discipline and have [3] at least eight years' experience in a regulated industry. [4] fluency in German is not essential, it would be viewed as a considerable advantage given the volume of correspondence with the Munich office.

questions.explanation: 'Collaborate closely with' departments is the natural collocation for joint work; 'cooperate' and 'coordinate' are less idiomatic here and 'correspond' means to write or match, not to work together.

choices: This is a senior post with direct influence on the company's recruitment, and it demands someone who is comfortable with routine.
This is a senior post with direct influence on the company's strategy, and it demands someone who is comfortable with ambiguity.
This is a junior post with limited influence on the company's strategy, and it demands someone who is comfortable with supervision.
This is a senior post that has been vacant since the company's strategy was revised, and it demands someone who started last year.
questions.explanation: The following sentence ('You will be expected to anticipate changes ... advise the executive board') describes a strategic, autonomous role. Only the first sentence prepares it: the others describe routine, a junior position or a vacancy.
'Have accumulated at least eight years' experience' needs the past participle after 'have'; the other forms are ungrammatical.
'Although fluency in German is not essential, it would be ...' expresses concession; the others express cause or condition and make no sense with the contrast that follows.

text:
Orbis Cloud Services – Service Level Commitments

Orbis guarantees that its hosted applications will be available for 99.95 percent of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least five days in advance. Availability is measured by an independent monitoring system, the results of which are published on the customer portal.

[1] Where availability falls below the guaranteed level, customers are entitled to a service credit calculated as a proportion of the monthly fee. [2] the shortfall exceed four hours, the credit is doubled. Claims must be submitted within thirty days of the incident; thereafter, they will not be [3]. The credits described above constitute the customer's sole remedy for [4] of the availability commitment.

choices: Failure to meet that standard therefore carries a financial consequence for Orbis rather than for customers.
Customers who experience interruptions must therefore bear the cost of any resulting losses themselves, without recourse.
Scheduled maintenance will therefore be counted as downtime for the purposes of the calculation described above.
Service credits will therefore be unavailable to customers during the first year of their subscription period.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says customers 'are entitled to a service credit' when availability falls short, so the previous sentence must say that failure costs the provider. The others contradict the text: customers bear losses, maintenance counts as downtime (it is excluded), or credits are unavailable.

'Should the shortfall exceed four hours' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if the shortfall exceeds'; 'whereas', 'although' and 'albeit' cannot take the subjunctive 'exceed' or introduce a condition.
A claim that is late 'will not be entertained', meaning considered; 'entailed' means involved, 'entrusted' means assigned, and 'enacted' means made into law.
A failure to meet the commitment is a 'breach' of it; 'breadth', 'brink' and 'breeding' cannot follow 'remedy for' with that meaning.
